summary: Build practical absence management and well-being skills with tools, case exercises, and leadership-ready reporting. Enrol today.
lede: Managing absenteeism and employee well-being involves measuring absence patterns and responding to recurring cases with consistent support. This course is for HR professionals, employee relations and occupational health staff, and managers responsible for attendance records or employee support. It covers calculating absence rates and Bradford Factor measures, analysing recurring patterns, and preparing return-to-work plans and well-being referral pathways, alongside confidentiality and case documentation.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who manage attendance data, support employee well-being, and handle recurring or long-term absence cases in real workplaces. HR Business Partners managing absence trends and manager escalation. Absence Management Specialists tracking triggers and return-to-work reviews. Employee Relations Officers handling recurring absence and case documentation. Line Managers applying attendance policy and support conversations. Occupational Health Coordinators linking referrals to fitness-for-work decisions. HR Analytics Specialists building absence dashboards and KPI reports. People Managers overseeing flexible work and workload-related absence risks. Well-being Program Managers coordinating support and referral pathways. Payroll and HR Operations Analysts reconciling absence records and leave codes. Senior HR Managers reporting absence patterns and intervention outcomes to leadership.
prerequisites: Prerequisites required: working knowledge of HR operations, employee relations, or line management processes; familiarity with basic attendance records and reporting; no coding required. You should already handle or review sickness absence, return-to-work conversations, or employee support referrals in your role. The course is delivered at intermediate level, so advanced absence analytics or occupational health specialist knowledge is not required, but a practical understanding of policy application, manager escalation, and confidential employee data handling will help you apply the material quickly.
